To determine the cost of upgrading your email plan, you need to follow these steps:

1. Go to Premium Subscriptions in your Wix account.
2. Click on the More Actions icon next to the current plan you're using.
3. Select the Upgrade Plan option.
4. Choose the new plan you wish to purchase and select its subscription period.
5. After selecting, click Continue to Checkout.
6. Enter your payment details and click Submit Purchase.

The cost will be based on the full price of your current plan divided by the number of days in the chosen subscription period, multiplied by the remaining days in your current subscription period. This calculation is detailed in FAQs for more information.

3. Verify that your changes are being saved properly after making any adjustments, as saving is crucial for updates to take effect.

5. Consider refreshing your browser or clearing your cache and cookies, as sometimes these can interfere with page rendering.

rounds.answer: If your domain is connected to Wix via pointing, you will need to contact your domain host for assistance in adding the TXT record on their end. Your domain host has control over your domain records and can add the necessary TXT record required for verifying your domain with Google Workspace. Once this is done, you should be able to proceed with the verification process as outlined in the reference material for manually verifying your domain using a TXT record.

If your domain is connected to Wix via pointing, you will need to contact your domain host for assistance in adding the TXT record on their end. Your domain host has control over your domain records and can add the necessary TXT record required for verifying your domain with Google Workspace. Once this is done, proceed as follows: 

1. Copy the specific TXT record provided by Google (e.g., "_acme-challenge.example.com" with a value like "V2gYR8QkHwqWz653P4mMnJZG9jTc7CtKfFpXxu0o"). 
2. Add this TXT record to your domain's DNS settings.
3. After adding the TXT record, you should be able to verify your domain using Google Workspace.

Additionally, if you have not already done so, add the following MX records for Google Workspace:
- Name/Host/Alias: @
- Time to Live (TTL): 86400
- Record Type: MX
- Priority Value/Answer/Destination: 1 ASPMX.L.GOOGLE.COM.
- 5 ALT1.ASPMX.L.GOOGLE.COM.
- 5 ALT2.ASPMX.L

If you're unable to access your old email address and need to update your password, you can use your recovery phone number to recover your account. Here are the steps:

1. Go to the Wix Sign In window.
2. Click on the "Forgot Password" or "Email?" link.
3. Select "Can't access my login email."
4. Enter the email address associated with your Wix account and click Next.
5. Choose "Send me a code to my phone number ending with XXXX" and then click Next.
6. Enter the one-time verification code sent to your mobile phone, and click "Verify."

After verifying your phone number, you will be able to reset your password using the new method of recovery.

2. Click the More Actions icon next to the admin email associated with your second Gmail account.

To create custom hours for a staff member in your Wix site's work schedule, follow these steps:

1. Go to your site dashboard and navigate to the Staff tab.
2. Select the specific staff member whose working hours you want to customize.
3. Click on "Edit" next to the relevant staff member's name.
4. Choose "Add Working Hours" from the options available.
5. Set a Start Date for these custom work hours if needed, and choose whether they should be temporary (set an end date) or permanent.
6. Select the days of the week that apply to these custom hours.

1. Go to Booking Services in your site's dashboard.
2. Click Manage Categories from the options provided.
3. You will see an option to + Add New Category. Enter the name for your new category and click "Add" to save it.

- Click Manage Categories at the top of the list.
- Drag and drop the categories into your preferred order using the drag handles next to them.

- You can also reorder services within their respective categories by clicking on the drag handle near the service name.

Remember that you cannot reorder all categories at once; you must do so individually. If needed, you can create new categories using the + Add New Category option available at the bottom of the list.

To update the og:image for your entire site, you should navigate to your Wix site's settings and select "Website settings." Scroll down to find the section labeled "General social image" and click on "Upload Image." Select the new image you wish to use from your library or upload a new one. After making this change, it will be applied across all pages of your site.

Regarding whether updating the og:image for your entire site affects its appearance when shared in an email or on Instagram, the answer is no. The og:image feature applies specifically to social media platforms like Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn, and others where Wix automatically generates a preview image based on the content of the page being shared. This does not affect how images are displayed in emails or on other platforms such as Instagram, which have their own specific settings for sharing content.

To create a custom sign-up form that links to your Members Area on your site, follow these steps:

1. **Access the Editor**: Open your Wix website editor by clicking on "Pages" and then selecting "Signup & Login".

2. **Select Member Signup Form**:
   - Click on "Member Signup Form (Default)".
   - Choose "Custom Form" from the dropdown menu under "Which member signup form do your visitors see?".

3. **Add Custom Elements**: 
   - You can add any element to your custom sign-up form, including buttons and images.
   - To customize an existing element, click on it and select "Edit Field".

4. **Design Your Form**:
   - Click the Design icon to choose a preset design for your form or click "Customize Design" to make further changes like text alignment and direction.

5. **Add Email Notification Settings**: 
   - Navigate to "Form Settings", then click on "Email Notifications".
   - Configure how you want to be notified when a new member signs up, including collaborators who will receive notifications.

6. **Save Your Form**:
   - After customizing your form according to the above steps, click "Add to Site" to save and publish it.

To allow customers to personalize their shirts by adding their names, you can follow these steps:

2. Select the relevant product or click "New Product" if you need to create a new one.
3. Scroll down until you see an option to add a custom text field. Click on this option.
4. Enter the title of the text field, for example, "What name should we engrave?"
5. Set the character limit for the text field as needed; ensure it accommodates names of varying lengths.
6. Decide whether or not you want customers to fill in this text field by default (mandatory). You can leave this unchecked if allowing them to skip is preferred.
7. Click "Add Another" to add a second custom text field, if necessary, for additional customization options.
8. After completing the above steps, click "Save."

These settings will enable customers to enter their names when purchasing the product, adding personalization to your shirts as desired.

1. Ensure your site is set up for testing by enabling the manual payment method and logging into your Members Area.

For processing a refund for a recurring payment made by a customer through Wix Payments, you should follow these steps:

1. Go to the Payments section in your site's dashboard.
2. Locate and click on the specific recurring payment transaction that needs to be refunded.
3. Click on the Refund button associated with this transaction.
4. Enter the amount of the refund and provide any necessary notes.
5. Confirm the refund by clicking the appropriate "Refund" or "Issue Refund" option.

If the option to refund does not appear, you will need to contact your payment provider directly for assistance in issuing the refund. Remember that refunds may take up to 3-5 business days to reach the customer's credit card/bank account and can be subject to processing fees charged by the payment provider.

To transfer your domain to another host, you should follow these steps:

1. Go to Domains in your Wix account.
2. Click on the Domain Actions icon next to the relevant domain.
3. Select Transfer away from Wix.
4. After reviewing the info about transferring your domain, click Transfer Domain.
5. Click I Still Want to Transfer.
6. We'll send a transfer authorization code (EPP code) to your domain's registrant contact email address.

Once you receive the EPP code, follow the instructions provided by your new domain host to complete the transfer process.

To unpublish your site, you can do this either through the Wix Editor or directly from your site's dashboard:

1. **From the Wix Editor**:
   - Open your site in the Wix Editor.
   - Select "Site" from the top toolbar.
   - Click on "Unpublish Site".
   - Confirm by clicking "Unpublish" in the pop-up window.

2. **From Your Site's Dashboard**:
   - Go to your site’s dashboard.
   - Navigate to “Settings” and then select “Website settings”.
   - At the top of the page, click on "Unpublish".
   - Confirm by clicking "Unpublish" again in the pop-up window.

After unpublishing, you'll still have access to your site's editor and can publish it again at any time. If you want to hide your site from search engines without completely unpublished it, you can also do this from your site’s dashboard under Search Engine Optimization (SEO) settings by disabling the "Let search engines index my site" toggle.

7. You can also customize additional aspects such as scroll behavior and image hover effects.

I understand you're experiencing issues applying a 50% off coupon on your Wix Store. Here are some troubleshooting steps to help resolve the problem:

1. Ensure that the promo code visibility is set correctly:
   - Go to Pages & Menu in your editor.
   - Select My site has only Wix Stores and then click Store Pages, followed by Cart Page.
   - Click Settings and make sure the Promo code link checkbox is selected.
   - Choose a color for the promo code link that contrasts with the background of your cart page.

2. Verify if the coupon is activated:
   - Navigate to Coupons in your site's dashboard.
   - Check if the 50% off coupon you created is enabled and not expired.

3. Confirm the usage limit hasn't been reached:
   - In the same Coupons tab, ensure there are no limits set for this specific coupon.

4. Double-check that the coupon code was entered correctly (case sensitive):
   - Make sure your customer entered the correct code without any case differences.

5. Ensure it's applicable to all products or a specific category:
   - Navigate to Coupons and select the 50% off coupon.
   - Check what is selected from the Apply to drop-down: All products or Specific product

To determine which PayPal account is connected to your Wix site, you can follow these steps:

1. Go to the Accept Payments section in your Wix dashboard.
2. Click on Manage next to PayPal (or any other payment provider if applicable).
3. In the Account Information section, you will see details about the current PayPal account associated with your site.

If you want to switch to a different PayPal account connected to the same provider, follow these steps:

1. Go to Accept Payments in your Wix dashboard.
2. Click on Manage next to the payment provider (in this case, PayPal).
3. Enter the email address of the desired PayPal account in the Account Information section and click Save.

If you're still unsure or encounter any issues during this process, consider reaching out to PayPal support for further assistance.

To create an automation for a standard Wix form, you can follow these steps:

1. Navigate to your site's dashboard and go to the Automations section.
2. Click on "+ New Automation" to start creating a new automation.
3. Choose "Wix Forms" as the trigger type since you're using a standard Wix form.
4. In the Trigger section, select "Form submitted" from the options available for selecting which forms trigger this automation.
5. Select your specific form(s) that use input elements and submit to a CMS collection.
6. Decide on how often the action should be triggered by setting the frequency in the Limit frequency drop-down menu (e.g., Don't limit, Once per contact).
7. Add any conditions if needed for more precise automation targeting.
8. Choose an appropriate action from the available options such as sending an email, creating a task, or updating contacts.
9. Customize your action details including sender information and template settings if necessary.
10. Click "Activate" to save and activate your new Wix form automation.

Remember that you can also customize existing suggested automations by clicking on them and making changes in the Trigger section.

If you've already checked the automation statistics and still haven't received your automated email, there are a few other steps you can take to troubleshoot this issue:

1. **Check Spam Folder**: Ensure the recipient's inbox is not filtering the email into their spam folder.
2. **Whitelist Emails**: If the email isn't in the spam folder, it might be due to being flagged as an unwanted sender by the recipient's email provider. Whitelist the following emails:
   - `no-reply@test.wixshoutout.com`
   - If you haven't set a confirmed reply-to email: `@automations.ascendbywix.com`
   - If you have set a confirmed reply-to email, whitelist your own email address.
3. **Verify Email Address**: Confirm that the recipient's email address is active and they've subscribed to your mailing list. The "SUBSCRIBED" label on their contact card indicates this status.

If after these steps the automated email still isn't sent, consider checking if there are any other conditions or settings in your automation that might be preventing it from executing, such as delays or limits set for frequency of execution.

If your emails sent through Wix Email Marketing are being marked as spam or not received by recipients, you should review and implement the best practices outlined in the Wix Email Marketing Best Practices guide. Here are some key steps:

1. **Maintain a Clean Email List**: Regularly remove inactive subscribers from your list to ensure it remains up-to-date and free of invalid email addresses.

2. **Avoid Spammy Language**: Ensure that your emails do not contain spammy language or content, such as excessive use of all caps, exclamation marks, or overly promotional text.

3. **Regularly Remove Unengaged Subscribers**: Use tools like campaign statistics to identify and remove recipients who consistently bounce or remain unopened over time. 

4. **Use a Subscribe Form on Your Site**: Make it easy for people to join your mailing list by adding a subscribe form to your site, which can help build an engaging audience for your campaigns.

5. **Monitor Sender Reputation**: Utilize tools like Postmaster Tools by Google to monitor and improve your sender reputation among ISPs and anti-spam organizations.

6. **Avoid Spam Traps**: Ensure that you do not send emails to addresses that are known spam traps, which can lead to penalties or restrictions on future campaigns.

If your site is unable to provide a secure connection, it's likely due to issues with your DNS records or SSL certificate. Here are steps you can take:

1. **Verify Your DNS Records**: Ensure that your domain's DNS settings are correctly configured and have propagated. You should check the A record pointing to 185.230.63.107, as well as any CNAME records for www if applicable.

2. **Check Your SSL Certificate**: Make sure you have a valid SSL certificate in place. If your domain is hosted by Wix, the SSL certificate should be automatically issued within 48 hours of updating DNS settings. Check that your A and CNAME records are set correctly with your domain host for this to work.

3. **Wait for Propagation**: Sometimes it takes up to 24-48 hours for changes made in DNS settings to propagate across the network, so wait for these changes to take effect before testing again.

4. **Review Domain Status and Security Settings**: Ensure that your domain is active and not flagged as expired or suspended by its registrar. Also, confirm that DNSSEC (Domain Name System Security Extensions) isn't signed if you're using a non-Wix domain.

5. **Clear

To resolve the issue of your site not appearing in search engine results, you should first verify that your site is properly indexed by Google through the Google Search Console or Bing Webmaster Tools. Once verified, submit a sitemap for your website via Google Search Console to help speed up the indexing process.

Next, ensure that your site's name appears correctly in search results by updating the og:site_name tag within your Wix editor. This can be done by navigating through Pages & Menu > More Actions > SEO Basics > Advanced SEO > Additional tags and editing the Tag value for og:site_name.

Additionally, make sure that your site is allowed to be indexed by checking the "Let search engines index my site" option in your SEO settings under Tools and Settings. This can also be accessed through your editor or via the SEO Dashboard.

Lastly, if you have not already done so, consider implementing proper redirects for any old URLs on your website using Wix's URL Redirect Manager to prevent any broken links from affecting search engine rankings.

By addressing these areas of your site’s SEO and ensuring it is properly indexed by search engines, you should see improvements in its visibility.

To adjust the image settings for your mobile site, follow these steps:

1. Open your Wix editor and navigate to your mobile site.
2. Click on the "Background" icon located on the left side of the mobile editor interface.
3. From there, click on "Image" to select the standalone image you want to adjust.
4. In the settings section that appears, you can change the opacity by dragging the slider provided. This will lighten the image if it's too dark.
5. You can also choose a color behind your image from the Color Picker option. Selecting a lighter color can help brighten up the image as well.
6. If needed, you can adjust the scroll effect to ensure your background remains in place while scrolling through your mobile site.

By following these steps, you should be able to lighten and enhance the visibility of your standalone image on your mobile site.

rounds.answer: Google Ads with Wix uses a monthly subscription model for all campaigns run through the platform. This means that the amount billed each month covers the total available ad credits across all campaigns within your account. If you want to purchase additional ad credit, you can do so with a one-time payment which is then added to your existing account balance. Any remaining ad credits from your monthly subscription will be carried over to the next billing cycle. When you pause a campaign, any associated ad credits remain in your account and are not immediately removed; they only expire if there's an expiry date on them while the campaign is paused.

To add new bank details to your Wix Payments account, follow these steps:

1. Go to the Accept Payments section in your site's dashboard.
2. Click on Wix Payments from the list of available services.
3. Click on Manage next to Wix Payments.
4. Click on Edit Account Details.
5. Update the relevant information for your bank details and click Save.

Note: After updating your account settings, you may need to go through a verification process which can take up to 7 business days. During this time, while you can accept payments on your site, you won't be able to receive payouts to your bank account.

2. Click Connect next to the desired payment provider (e.g., Wix Payments).

- Click Connect Existing Account and follow the instructions to connect your existing account.

Make sure to complete your account set-up in order to get paid to your bank account.

If you are unable to locate the cancellation option for your Wix Premium plan within the first 14 days due to auto-renewal settings, you should follow these steps:

1. Go to your account dashboard in Wix.
2. Navigate to "Premium Subscriptions" from the menu options.
3. Find and click on the relevant plan that needs cancellation.
4. Look for an option labeled "Show More Actions," which may be represented by three dots or a downward arrow icon.
5. Click on this action, then select "Cancel Plan."
6. Confirm your decision to cancel by clicking "Cancel Now."

If you still cannot find these options, it might be due to the auto-renewal setting. To turn off the automatic renewal:
- Go to Premium Subscriptions in your account.
- Find and click on the plan that needs cancellation.
- Click the Show More icon next to the relevant plan.
- Choose "Cancel Plan."
- Confirm by clicking "Cancel Now."

Remember, if you cancel within the first 14 days of a monthly subscription, you will receive a full refund. However, for yearly plans, the refund period is typically up to 20 business days after cancellation.

For your questions regarding your Google Ads campaign with Wix:

1. Your paid ad may not immediately appear in the campaign list after it has been reviewed by Wix and Meta. This process can take anywhere from 24 hours to a few days, depending on how quickly your account is processed.

If there's not enough credit available to cover a particular day's spend, your account may be charged for that day.

To ensure your paid ads appear correctly:
- Check if you have any paused or live campaigns.
- Make sure your campaign is set up with an appropriate daily budget and ad credits subscription.
- Review the Wix dashboard regularly for updates on your campaigns' status and performance. 

For automatic credit top-ups, review your account settings to ensure auto-renewal is enabled. This will prevent your subscription from expiring before you have spent enough to cover any remaining days of ad credits.

To go back to the history of your Wix site, you can access your site history from either the Editor or your site's dashboard. Here are the steps:

1. **From the Editor**:
   - Click on the Site icon located at the top of the Editor.

   - Navigate to the Site & Mobile App tab within your site’s dashboard.

- Click the Arrow icon next to the version you want to view.
- Review the revision to ensure it is the one you wish to restore.
- Click Restore.

To clear your browser's cache, you should follow these general steps:

For most browsers (like Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge):
- Open a new tab in your browser.
- Press `Ctrl + Shift + Del` or `Cmd + Shift + Delete` on your keyboard to open the cache clearing dialog.
- Select "All time" as the time range for deletion.
- Ensure that "Cached images and files" is checked.
- Click "Clear data."

For Safari:
- Open a new tab in your browser.
- Press `Cmd + ,` to open Preferences.
- Go to the Advanced tab, then check the box next to Show Develop menu in menu bar (at the bottom of the window).
- Click Develop in Safari's menu bar and select Empty Caches.
- Close and reopen Safari.

These steps should clear your browser cache. If you're still experiencing issues after clearing the cache, consider flushing your DNS or disabling extensions/cookies as suggested in the reference context.

2. Click on Settings in the left sidebar menu.
3. Select Website Settings from the dropdown menu.
4. Under Site History, click Restore Versions.
5. Use the list to find the Wix Editor version you want to restore and click the Arrow icon next to it to restore that specific revision.

To update a site from the Wix Editor to the Wix Studio Editor, you need to follow these steps:

1. Open the relevant site in the Wix Editor.
2. In the pop-up that appears when you open the editor, click on "Next."
3. Click on "Update to Wix Studio" within the pop-up.

After clicking "Update to Wix Studio," your site will be updated and moved over to the new Wix Studio Editor within minutes. However, note that not all features of the Wix Editor are available in the Wix Studio Editor, so you may need to rebuild parts of your site using the new editor's capabilities.

If you have any existing sites created with the Wix Editor, they will eventually be updated to the Wix Studio Editor as part of a gradual rollout. Starting April 2024, it won't be possible to create new sites on the Wix Editor; instead, all future projects should be done in the Wix Studio Editor.

If you encounter issues with updating your site, ensure that no other editor tabs are open and that only the site owner can perform this update.

Yes, you can hide a page from appearing in your site's main menu and search results while still providing a direct link for visitors to access the hidden page. To do this:

1. Go to your Wix Editor.
2. Click on "Pages & Menu" located on the left side of the editor panel.
3. Find the page you want to hide from appearing in the main site menu and click on its More Actions icon (usually represented by three dots).
4. Select "Hide from menu." This will remove the page from your site's main navigation but it won't be hidden from search engines automatically.

If you need to prevent search engines from indexing this page as well, follow these additional steps:

1. Click on "SEO Basics" located in the More Actions dropdown for that specific page.
2. Uncheck the box labeled "Let search engines index this page."

By hiding a page from your main menu and disabling search engine indexing, you can still provide visitors with direct links to access the hidden content.

If you're experiencing difficulties connecting your Instagram business account to your Wix site, and the instructions suggest clearing your browser's cookies as a solution, here’s what you should do:

1. Open your web browser (e.g., Chrome, Firefox, Safari).
2. Click on the three horizontal lines in the top right corner of the browser window to open the menu.
3. Select "Settings" or "Preferences," depending on your browser version.
4. Scroll down and find an option called "Privacy and security" or "Cookies and other site data."
5. Here, you should see a section for managing cookies. Click on it.
6. You may have options to clear browsing data, including cookies. Choose this option and select the time range (e.g., all time) when you want to clear your cookies.
7. After clearing your cookies, try connecting your Instagram account to your Wix site again.

If you continue to encounter issues after clearing your browser's cookies, it might be helpful to disconnect and reconnect both your Instagram business account and the Wix Apps business integration in your Facebook settings as suggested in step 6 of the troubleshooting guide.

If you're encountering a 403 error message on your Wix site, it typically indicates that Google Search Console is unable to access the page due to restrictions or issues with server configuration. Here are steps to resolve this issue:

1. **Check URL and Permissions**: Ensure that the URL you are trying to modify is correct and that there are no password-protected areas or member-only settings that might be causing the 403 error.

2. **Clear Browser Cache and Cookies**: Sometimes, cached data can interfere with page access. Clear your browser's cache and cookies before attempting to access the site again.

3. **Review Google Search Console Settings**:
   - Log into your Google Search Console account.
   - Check for any pages that are marked as restricted or password-protected in your Site Visibility report.
   - If you find such restrictions, remove them so that Google can crawl and index the page correctly.

4. **Verify Robots.txt File**: Ensure that there are no entries in your site's robots.txt file blocking access to the specific page causing issues.

5. **Contact Wix Support**: If after checking these steps the issue persists, it might be helpful to contact Wix support for further assistance. They can help diagnose and resolve server-side configuration issues

To adjust the positioning of your images using the Toolbar and Layers Panel in the Wix Editor:

Using the Toolbar:
1. Click on the Tools icon at the top right corner of the editor.
2. From the dropdown menu, select the "Toolbar" option to display it on the right side of the editor.
3. Use the toolbar's positioning tools such as dragging elements left or right (X value) and up or down (Y value) to adjust your image's position.

Using the Layers Panel:
1. Click on the Layers icon at the bottom-left corner of the editor to open the Layers panel.
2. In the Layers panel, locate the images you want to move by their ID number in the "ID" column.
3. Select the image(s) you wish to adjust and drag them up or down within the panel to change their order and position on your page.

Both methods allow for precise adjustments of your image's positioning; however, using both together can provide a more comprehensive approach when needed.

2. Select an option for either Edit a default rule or Add Region based on whether you already have a region setup or need to create one.
3. Once the region is selected, proceed to set up the Flat Rate shipping Rule.
4. Choose Flat Rate from the "Select how shipping is calculated" drop-down menu.
5. Enter a name for your flat rate in the "Shipping Option Name" field (e.g., Standard Shipping).
6. Optionally, you can enter an estimated delivery time and specify the flat rate fee in the respective fields.
7. If you want to offer free shipping on orders above a specific amount, check the "Offer Free Shipping when customer buys over a certain amount" checkbox and set the price threshold accordingly.

By following these steps, you will successfully configure a flat rate shipping rule for your Wix online store.

To connect elements on your dynamic item page to the correct fields in your CMS collection using Wix Editor, follow these steps:

1. Go to the Add panel within the Editor.
2. Click on the element you wish to add (such as an image or text box).
3. In the Editor, select the element you just added.
4. Click on the Connect to Data icon (or click the Connect to Data button in Editor X if using that version of Wix Editor).
5. Under the "Connect a dataset" section, choose the appropriate collection field from your CMS where you want this element's data to be displayed.
6. For elements like text boxes or images, under the "Connection Options" section, select what you wish to connect each field in the selected collection to (e.g., Text, Number, Date and Time, Address, Tags).
7. Repeat steps 4-6 for any additional elements on your page.

Remember that not all elements have connection options; some may require a different approach or additional settings depending on their type.
For more specific guidance, refer to the CMS: Adding Additional Dynamic Item Pages for a Collection article in the reference context provided.

To prevent an item in your CMS collection from being published to your website until it's completed, you should set its status to "Hidden." Here are the steps:

1. Go to your site's editor.
2. Click on CMS on the left side of the editor.
3. Navigate to Your Collections.
4. Locate and click on the relevant collection where items are stored.
5. Find the item for which you want to set the status to "Hidden."
6. Click on the Status field for that specific item.
7. Select "Hidden" from the dropdown menu.

By setting the item's status to "Hidden," it will not appear on your live site until its completion, ensuring that only fully completed items are published.

1. Double-check that the Business Number or Tax ID/EIN you provided matches exactly with what is registered on your business bank account.
2. If possible, obtain a document from your registrar of companies (or equivalent) that confirms the validity and ownership of the company number you're using for verification purposes.    - After making your changes, don't forget to save them by clicking on the "Save" button located at the top or bottom of the Wix Editor interface.
